title: Personal Factor Contribution
description: Calculate your personal economic contribution to the economy through labor (wages), human capital development (education), and capital provision (savings), understanding how YOU are a factor of production earning income.
learning_objectives: Calculate current or projected labor income based on wage rates and hours worked
Understand how human capital investments increase earning potential
Calculate interest earned from savings as capital contribution to the economy
Project future income based on educational and skill development plans
Connect personal financial decisions to factors of production concepts
instructions: Enter your current job or target career and hourly wage (or use minimum wage as baseline)
Input hours worked per week to calculate weekly and annual labor income
Check all human capital investments that apply (education, certifications, skills)
Enter current savings amount and interest rate to calculate capital income
Click 'Calculate My Factor Contribution' to see your total economic contribution
Review projections showing how human capital development increases future earnings
Reflect on insights about maximizing your economic value
materials_needed: Wage and salary data for common jobs
Human capital boost percentages by education level

low_income_student.message: Your current labor income is modest. Consider investing in education or skills training to boost your human capital and earning potential.
low_income_student.recommendation: Focus on developing skills that increase your hourly wage rate

moderate_income_student.message: Solid income foundation! Growing your human capital through certifications or advanced training could significantly boost your earnings.
moderate_income_student.recommendation: Look for specialized certifications in your field

high_income_potential.message: Strong earning potential! Consider diversifying income sources by building capital (savings/investments) to earn interest alongside wages.

reflection_prompts.prompt: Which factor of production do YOU currently provide (or will provide) to earn income?
reflection_prompts.expected_answer: Labor - through working at a job
reflection_prompts.teaching_point: Most people earn income primarily from labor (wages) until they build capital

reflection_prompts.prompt: How could you increase your 'human capital' to earn higher wages?
expected_answers: Complete college degree or certification program
Learn technical skills through training or online courses
Gain work experience in specialized field
Develop soft skills like communication and leadership

reflection_prompts.prompt: If you saved $10,000 and put it in a savings account earning 4% interest, which factor of production are you providing?
reflection_prompts.expected_answer: Capital - your savings become capital that businesses borrow and use
reflection_prompts.teaching_point: Savers are capital providers, earning interest as their factor payment

deliverables: Calculated current labor income (weekly and annual)
Identified human capital investments and calculated total wage boost
Calculated capital contribution from savings and interest earned
Projected future income with full human capital development
Personal plan for maximizing economic contribution and earnings

criteria: Correctly calculated labor income from wage and hours inputs
Identified relevant human capital investments and understood their impact on earnings
Calculated interest earned from savings as capital contribution
Connected personal financial decisions to factors of production framework
Developed realistic plan for increasing earning potential

teacher_notes: This activity makes economics deeply personal. Students realize THEY are factors of production earning income. Emphasize that labor is their current primary income source, but human capital development dramatically increases labor value. Even small savings contribute capital to the economy and earn interest. The human capital boost percentages are conservative estimates - actual wage premiums can be higher. Encourage students to see education as an investment in their most valuable asset: themselves. Note that the calculator respects student privacy - no data is collected or stored.
